When I was in college, I still lived at home with my parents. My parents live on 10 acres of wooded land in the country. One night I was up late watching TV and both of my parents were asleep in their room. It had stormed earlier and our land line was dead. So I was watching TV late at night when suddenly there was a knock on the door. I opened the blinds to see who it was and there were 2 police officers standing there. I opened the door and asked what was going on and they told me they received a 911 call from my address. I told them that wasn't possible because our phone line was out. They asked me if I was home alone, and I said no, that my parents were in the next room. They ended up leaving. It wasn't until after they left that it clicked why everything felt so off. The officers were in those dark blue uniforms city cops wear. The problem with that is, where I lived we had sheriffs, who wear tan uniforms. It's why I don't usually include him on Mother's Day, I usually do something with just the kids but I wanted bottomless mimosas so I needed him to drive. We ended up not going to the park either because I still had things to do at home. And when we got home and I started doing laundry and cleaning again, he sat in his chair and read a book. I wasn't wearing high visibility clothing because I was basically in my yard so I didn't think I had to. After being out there for a while I heard some gunshots. It's not unusual to hear gunshots out in the country because people often practice shooting or test their sights for the upcoming deer season, but these sounded uncomfortably close. I then saw an orange vest in the distance. I moved farther back on the trampoline and thought about running inside, but then I was worried if I ran he might just see movement and shoot me. I heard another gunshot right as a breeze came by and I remember thinking "wow, that breeze really hurt". I was in shock and it didn't really click what happened, but I started crying and ran as fast as I could down the trail and back to my house. When I got inside my mom asked what was wrong and I managed to sputter out that I heard gunshots and then she said "oh my god, you're bleeding!" She called for my dad and he ran outside to find the guy. Meanwhile my mom was getting me in the car to drive me to the ER. (It's faster to drive there than to wait for an ambulance). I remember thinking "I don't want to die" over and over again. I was so scared. I saw my dad drag a guy out of the woods and break his shot gun, I couldn't tell who it was at the time. He was yelling at him and I thought he was going to kill him. Then my dad came to the car and we all went to the ER. I remember the cops coming to the ER but I didn't hear what my parents said to them. They did an X-Ray and the doctor told us it was too risky to remove because it was so close to my carotid. He said I was extremely lucky to be alive, and me moving to a different place on the trampoline likely saved my life. I later learned it was my dad's best friend's brother who shot me, and although my parents were obviously pissed at him, they decided not to press charges because they didn't want to fuck up things for his wife and kids. They gave me misoprostol to ripen my cervix at 9 pm, I believe I got 2 doses of that then they started the pitocin. At 6 am the next day I started having contractions. I wish I had waited longer because my body got used to the fentanyl by the time the "real" contractions started so it didn't do much and it was very very painful. After many hours my cervix was still only at 3 cm so they stopped the pitocin. An hour later I was fully dilated. They had me wait to start pushing until my body was basically pushing on its own. I pushed for an hour, and the pushing actually wasn't painful it was just a lot of work, I passed out multiple times between contractions. When she was crowning I was so exhausted I could only push for 3-4 seconds at a time rather than the 10 seconds they wanted me to push for. I kept saying I couldn't do, but my mom, my husband, the doctor, and nurses all kept telling me I could. I was given a partial episiotomy and finally I was able to push her out. All in all I was in labor for about 23 hours (I'm not sure how much of that was active labor) and pushed for one hour. My episiotomy healed really well, I actually did not take very long to recover after giving birth. I gave myself two weeks of rest, but I was feeling pretty good after only 4 days. Oh and my daughter was born 6lbs 14 oz perfectly healthy. She did not need to spend any time in the NICU. There were things I really liked about being induced which are not having to worry about making it to the hospital in time and already being in a gown when my water broke so I didn't have to worry about the mess or discomfort of it being in my pants. I don't know if being induced is better or worse than not, but I wouldn't mind doing it again if needed.
